A1.justification: Both PDFs describe X-Scene, with matching authors, core architecture and retained experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original occupancy and image-generation results, downstream training experiments, component ablations and qualitative scene-generation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds video-generation and planning evaluations, supplementary ablations, robustness and efficiency measurements, and a human preference study.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 adds motion-aware video diffusion to the retained occupancy-image pipeline. The extension introduces temporal self-attention, reference-frame features, relative ego-pose conditioning, temporal-layer fine-tuning and autoregressive video inference. This substantially expands the generation procedure beyond v1's static scenes.

E1.justification: The datasets remain nuScenes and Occ3D-nuScenes, but v2 adds dynamic multi-view video generation and end-to-end planning evaluation using trajectory error and collision rates. Appendix C also evaluates corrupted layouts, adding an input-degradation scenario absent from v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding original experiments. The new video comparison reuses MagicDrive and DreamForge, already evaluated in v1. The additional appendix comparisons concern internal ablations and controls, without introducing a new external comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantial protocols for its new experiments: video interpolation from 2 Hz to 12 Hz, seven-frame training, FVD and UniAD perception/planning evaluation, Gaussian layout perturbations with 25% probability, and a study involving ten participants and 100 scene pairs. The original 700/150 scene split and retained experiment settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests removal of spatial conditioning, semantic versus vector layouts, propagation of layout noise, stage-wise inference efficiency, and generation with versus without RAG. These directly investigate conditioning, robustness and component utility beyond v1's retained occupancy and image-component ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new human study supplies participant/sample counts and preference percentages, but introduces no uncertainty estimates or statistical testing.

E6.justification: The original quantitative results are retained. New Table 4 reports video FVD of 179.7 for X-Scene, 217.9 for MagicDrive and 209.9 for DreamForge, alongside perception and planning results; training clip budgets differ. Tables 10–14 add substantial findings, including text-only FID of 20.74 versus 11.29 and overall RAG preference of 77% versus 23%.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a formally specified video-denoising objective conditioned on reference features and relative ego poses, using the existing squared-error diffusion formulation. The original graph definitions, triplane-attention equation and outpainting mathematics remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the central contribution from aligned occupancy-image generation to unified occupancy-image-video generation with temporal coherence. Dynamic generation moves from an explicitly deferred capability in v1 to a claimed supported capability in v2.

C2.justification: v1's static-only limitation is replaced by discussion of autoregressive error accumulation, temporal drift and limited long-horizon synthesis in v2 Section 5 and Appendix E.2. New interpretations connect robustness to geometric alignment and RAG to grounded scene generation. The dataset-diversity and fixed-category limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds the video training and inference recipe, including reference-frame sampling, 100 training epochs, batch size eight, eight A100 GPUs, optimizer settings and autoregressive initialization. Appendix C adds stage-wise sampling steps, latency and GPU memory measurements. Existing occupancy/image implementation details and resource links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including NeuralFloors/++, Text2LiDAR, LiDARcrafter and a 3D/4D world-modeling survey, while retaining the main related-work taxonomy and comparison with manual-layout approaches. Positioning now includes temporal dynamics, and Section 3.2 removes the explicit statement that the generation hierarchy is inspired by UniScene.

P1.justification: Beyond the added scientific content, v2 substantially rewrites or condenses the abstract, introduction, related work, methodology overview, outpainting explanations, downstream discussion and conclusion. Numbered related-work subsections become compact paragraphs, and a new quantitative appendix reorganizes the supplementary narrative. Many detailed technical and prompt passages remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds an overview diagram, a video example grid, a video-evaluation table and five supplementary quantitative tables. The pipeline graphic is updated, and downstream and ablation tables are relocated. The earlier qualitative appendix figures are retained and renumbered, rather than replaced by new results.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's simulation and controllability aims. It addresses v1's acknowledged static-only boundary with a documented temporal module and video/planning evaluation, while Tables 10–14 directly test previously unisolated spatial controls, layout robustness and RAG utility. These additions improve empirical substantiation and reproducibility. Long-horizon drift remains acknowledged, and absent uncertainty estimates and incomplete noise/user-study details still limit the strength of some conclusions.
